batchName: Middle Republic: The Gracchi (133-121 BCE) - Latin words
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: In 133 BC Tiberius was elected tribunus plebis. What was that?
options: One of ten officials who protected ordinary citizens
questions.explanation: He used the office to propose his land law.
questions.sourceQuote: Tiberius Gracchus was elected tribune of the plebs (*tribunus plebis*), one of ten officials whose job was to protect ordinary citizens.

questions.question: Scipio Nasica, who led the mob against Tiberius, was pontifex maximus. What was that?
options: The chief priest, head of Rome’s state religion
questions.explanation: He framed the attack as a religious rite to rid Rome of a would-be tyrant.
questions.sourceQuote: Scipio Nasica, was chief priest (*pontifex maximus*), head of Rome's state religion.

questions.question: After crushing Gaius, Opimius built a temple to Concordia. Who was she?
questions.explanation: Someone carved: “A work of mad discord produces a temple of Concord.”
questions.sourceQuote: built a grand temple to the goddess Concord (*Concordia*), symbol of civic harmony

questions.question: What was the lex Sempronia agraria?
questions.explanation: It enforced an old limit of about 120 hectares on public land and gave the surplus to poor citizens.
questions.sourceQuote: His agrarian law (*lex Sempronia agraria*) would enforce that limit

questions.question: Where did Tiberius take his land bill, without consulting the Senate first?
questions.explanation: Custom expected him to consult the Senate first.
questions.sourceQuote: He took his bill straight to the Plebeian Council (*concilium plebis*)

questions.question: Gaius saw that Italy did not have enough land for everyone. What did he plan?
options: Coloniae, including one overseas at Carthage
A war to win land in Gaul
Buying land from the Italian allies
questions.explanation: In 121 BC a new tribune moved to cancel the colony at Carthage.
questions.sourceQuote: so he planned colonies (*coloniae*), new settlements of citizens, including one overseas at Carthage.

questions.question: As quaestor in Spain in 137 BC, what was Tiberius in charge of?
questions.explanation: He negotiated the deal that saved the army trapped by Numantia.
questions.sourceQuote: In 137 BC he went to Spain as a quaestor (*quaestor*), a junior officer in charge of an army's finances.

questions.question: In 121 BC the Senate passed its first senatus consultum ultimum. What did it urge the consul to do?
options: Defend the state by any means necessary
questions.explanation: Opimius marched on the Gracchans on the Aventine; Gaius died across the Tiber.
questions.sourceQuote: It passed its first "final decree" (*senatus consultum ultimum*), urging him to defend the state by any means necessary.
